questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Please explain: *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The available courses and the reputation of the university

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Absolutely incredibly experience

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy. Almost everything had been sent the before arriving, and the little that hadn't was told to us in the intro days

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: In terms of residence at the university: none. However, everything was written in a mail which was highly informative and no problems arose. After that there were several intro days for new international students helping you be brought up to speed

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: No comments. Basically flawless

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer:
While I'm not sure i can make an exhaustive list (I'm under the impression there are quite a few different options), at campus Solna, where i was staying, you've got 3 huge apartments each filled with either:
* Shared 2-bedroom apartments where two tenants each have an own bedroom (single room) and share kitchen and bathroom.
* A private studio apartment with private kitchenette and bathroom.
* A studio apartment with own bathroom and refrigerator. The common kitchen is shared with other tenants on the same floor.
* There are shared 4-bedroom apartments where four tenants each have an own bedroom (single room) and share kitchen, living room and two bathrooms (this is what i did)

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer:
Every apartment was fully furnished and had classic utensils, pots, pans etc. 

It is pretty basic so don't expect any fancy kitchenware machines though

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer:
It is extremely easy: You'll live within 5-10 minutes of whereever your classes will be taking place. The rent is probably as good as it's gonna considering your other options in Stockholm. 

You receive conformation that your application has been approved quite late (I'm sure they have a good reason don't get me wrong). Somewhere around the middle of May assuming its the same next year.

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Because you'll live with your co-students in the same apartment, the ability to be social is absolutely incredible. It was a huge contributor to making my stay as amazing as i found it to be.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
Once you've arrived, i was are pre-registered to all your approved courses. i DID have to register for the exam as well but the lecturer made sure to mention and explain the process. 

You just log onto the website: "Ladok" (google: "Ladok KI"), click on your current course, and then "register". That's it. Very simple stuff

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I don't know, since it wasn't needed. Again, it was extremely easy

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: No problems at all. I should stress that i did the biomedicine programme for 2nd year students and that comes as a package of courrses. In other words, if you want to have just a single course, that's not gonna be possible (as far as i'm aware anyhow). You have to go through all courses associated with the semester.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Doublecheck on canvas and ladok that you are registered once you recieve your login information

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: To me, it felt like a *slight* step down from the university of Copenhagen. I'll go more into detail in other boxes

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
The level appropriate most of the time. 

You sometimes ran into the unfortunate situation of a researcher lecturing on something they've been working on for years, not really getting just how little we knew and how much they would need to slow down for people to grasp it.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
A few big differences:

For most courses, theres usually a new lecturer ever "subject"; e.g. a lecturer will teach you about T-cell for 3 hours and then you never see him again. This means you will meet A LOT of new lecturers as they will just constantly be introduced as leave. As one can imagine, there is quite a bit of varience here with some being great and others maybe being more suited for research.

Secondly, your hours were you attend lectures will be longer. During most courses, i was there from 9-16 5 days a week. In theory, there is also no book associated with most courses (aside from neuroscience). I loathed this personally, but it is very much a preference thing, and you can make it work even if you don't show up to every lecture. Most thing aren't mandatory

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Biostatistics
Tissue biology
Immunology and microbiology
Neuroscience

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Neuroscience was excellent. Good pace, an actual book to follow, practical lab was informative.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Free gym, tennis, badminton.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Too many to count, but I'll try:
* Running
* Bible studies
* Gym
* Tennis
* A good deal of parties
* More

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The Stockholm nobel light show in december was pretty good.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Karolinska doesn't do any other holidays than summer and christmas.

That aside, going up to see lapland during a weekend is recommended.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy. To be entirely honest, basically everyone in my course and apartment was international, so it is not like a had a huge amount of interaction with Swedes and swedish culture unless i actively "chased" it.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Go to events in the beginning. Then, start doing some activity routinely. This can be by joining a club, but even something as simple as a movie night can be great.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: No drinking in public, alcohol can only be bought in government stores and they close at 14:00 during weekends

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Individuality. People just mind their own business

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
* I cannot stress enough how much i would recommend getting an apartment on campus. Especially a shared 4-bedroom apartment.

* As you know, social circles tend to form early. Lock in on being prosocial and active during the first month

* Even if you don't have any holidays (christmas and summer aside), you can still make a lot happen during the weekends

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
I feel like i've covered it...

The library is open till 22, so use that when you are behind on your studies i guess?

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The people. I've met a bunch of people from pretty different background to my own, with whom i've had a great many good experiences. The social aspect really is special

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer:
Differences in teaching styles, meaning long days of complex lectures where i just wanted to read it in a book at my preffered hours.

Maybe the darkness? But again, I'm danish so its not that different

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: From what I've gathered, their research and internships are absolutely superb and probably where they really shine

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
